newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BRUSSELS BOURSE TRUDGES SIDEWAYS, SEEN RESTING.
newsitem.headline: BRUSSELS BOURSE TRUDGES SIDEWAYS, SEEN RESTING.

text.p: The Brussels stock market trudged sideways on Tuesday with no help from New York and players nervous of entering the market before the U.S. Federal Reserve Open Market Committee ends its two-day meeting on Wednesday.
Traders said that although there was no anticipation the Fed would raise interest rates at the meeting, it was unclear where the market would move once the results was known.

"We went up 10 percent in January so it is time to take a breather," one trader said. "But much depends on what happens in New York and that is very difficult to predict. The development of European fundamentals is also getting more attention."
In classic cases the Bel-20 share index would undergo a 50 percent correction after such a steep rally, which would take it back to around 1,970.
But traders noted that the market had already climbed from the dip to 2,031 it hit on January 29 and there was still a lot of money looking for a home.
This, they said, coupled with the underlying confident mood suggested that the market still had more upside potential -- at least in the near term.
The index ended Tuesday a scant 0.08 points up at 2,053.59 in an uninspired volume of 2.6 billion francs.
There were eight gainers, 10 losers and two unchanged in the index.
A key performer during the day was Kredietbank which lost 250 francs or 1.9 percent to 11,300 francs.

Traders said this was due to a combination of worries about questioning of officials on Monday by judicial police probing allegations of tax irregularities, and a simple downward correction after January speculation Belgium's fourth largest bank might be looking for partners.
Electronics firm Barco rose 180 francs or 3.1 percent to 5,940 francs on renewed market interest.

Traders also noted discount retailer chemical and drugs firm UCB which ended 250 francs down at 94,300 francs ahead of provisional annual results which are due to be announced after the close of play on Wednesday.
Chemical firm Solvay was a strong performer, rising 200 francs to 22,475 on market anticipation of an improving performance.
